subject: quotemeta escapes high bytes by Unicode \w, not perl's default byte semantics (op/quotemeta.t t30/t31)
description:
DECIDED s317 (fable-answers-s316v.md §6b): option (a) — default is perl's BYTE semantics (ASCII/Latin-1 \w); Unicode rules apply only under `use utf8` / `use feature 'unicode_strings'`, selected at TRANSPILE time from the pragma scope (no runtime per-string flag needed). Fix the not-supported.md Unicode sentence in the SAME commit. If other \w-sensitive builtins share p-quotemeta's helper, fix the helper once (CLAUDE.md 11) with per-builtin probes. Post-R1 (W2.5 queue).

op/quotemeta.t is perl 60/0 vs PCL 58/2; both failures are t30/t31 "quotemeta Latin1 no unicode_strings quoted" / "... quoted length".

  my $c = chr(0xe9);  my $q = quotemeta $c;
  perl: length 2, first char \  (the high byte IS escaped)
  PCL:  length 1, unescaped

ROOT — cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:2846 `p-quotemeta`, and it is deliberate-looking:
    For non-ASCII (code >= 128): escape unless Unicode alphanumeric (\w)
so `é` counts as a word char via CL `alphanumericp` and is left alone. Perl WITHOUT `use feature 'unicode_strings'` uses byte semantics: a high byte is not a word character, so quotemeta escapes it. With unicode_strings (or a UTF8-flagged string) perl does treat Latin-1 letters as word chars — the case the current code was written for, applied UNCONDITIONALLY.

DOC INACCURACY TO FIX ALONGSIDE: docs/not-supported.md §"Unicode semantics differences" currently asserts "Without the pragma, high bytes stay Latin-1 (byte semantics), matching Perl." quotemeta is a counter-example — the code, not the doc's intent, was wrong; correct the sentence when the fix lands.

Probe: scratchpad w0/q1.pl.
